title: Feature Request: PHP Filters for labels per post type
body:
## Feature Request

Add a filter for labels and post types for each label.

```
It would be nice if we could have some PHP hook to allow us to filter the different types of messages according to the post type.
Ex: A website can have both a blog and a shop section. In which case a "comment" should actually better be called a "review" in the product pages.
Currently doing it via your JS callbacks, by finding a body CSS class that belongs to the post type, and then overriding the appropriate WPAC._Options properties.
It would be much nicer if this could be done at PHP level.
```

## Describe any solutions you've considered

JS filtering.

## How important is this feature to you?

Important as it'll save some dev time for users.

1. Install and activate the plugin
2. Visit the Settings tab
3. Enable Ajaxify Comments and Save Options
4. Navigate to https://pagespeed.web.dev/
5. Enter the URL of your WordPress instance
6. Click Analyze


## Additional Comments
PageSpeed Insights output:

Registers an unload listener: 
The unload event does not fire reliably and listening for it can prevent browser optimizations like the Back-Forward Cache. Use pagehide or visibilitychange events instead.

title: Normalize PHP line endings and prevent CRLF whitespace noise
body:
## What

Normalize the plugin bootstrap PHP file to LF line endings and add a Git attribute that keeps PHP files on LF so future diffs do not report carriage returns as trailing whitespace.

## Why

At PR #18 head `bfeba15`, `git diff --check` reports trailing whitespace on the changed plugin header lines. The file is ASCII with CRLF line terminators, so otherwise valid edits create noisy whitespace failures.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `wp-ajaxify-comments.php`
- `.gitattributes`

### Reference Pattern

The existing `.gitattributes` contains one targeted whitespace rule for `src/js/frontend/wp-ajaxify-comments.js`. Add an explicit PHP text rule rather than changing or removing that existing JavaScript rule.

### Exact Transform

1. Convert `wp-ajaxify-comments.php` from CRLF to LF without changing PHP content.
2. Add `*.php text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes`.
3. Confirm that the content diff for `wp-ajaxify-comments.php`, when end-of-line whitespace is ignored, is empty.
4. Verify PHP syntax and repository whitespace checks.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not reformat, reorder, or otherwise modify the bootstrap file while normalizing it.
- Preserve the existing `.gitattributes` JavaScript rule.
- Keep the change narrowly scoped; do not mass-normalize unrelated tracked files in the same pull request.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wp-ajaxify-comments.php` uses LF line endings.
- [ ] `.gitattributes` enforces LF for tracked PHP files.
- [ ] The bootstrap file has no semantic content changes.
- [ ] `git diff --check` passes for the change.
- [ ] PHP syntax validation passes.

## Verification

```bash
file wp-ajaxify-comments.php
php -l wp-ajaxify-comments.php
git diff --ignore-space-at-eol -- wp-ajaxify-comments.php
git diff --check
```

The `--ignore-space-at-eol` diff for the bootstrap file should be empty after conversion; the only substantive diff should be the `.gitattributes` rule.

## Evidence

Observed on `bfeba1523a70fe44435939741131bb266d05942f`:

- `file wp-ajaxify-comments.php` reports `ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators`.
- `git diff --check` identifies header lines 9 through 12 as trailing whitespace when compared with the PR base.
- `.gitattributes` currently has no PHP line-ending rule.
